title: OneDrive Photos on Windows: policies for personal account sign-in and app blocking
summary: Hold: the Intune navigation skips required profile-creation and Basics steps before Configuration settings. The rollout and named policy effects are supported, but Microsoft does not establish that devices excluded from the update necessarily retain the previous Photos app.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The notice says the update is not installed on affected devices when the organisation disables or removes Store-originated apps using DisableStoreApps.
claims.quote: If your organization disables or removes Store-originated apps using DisableStoreApps, the update will not be installed on affected devices.

claims.claim: Devices excluded from the update by DisableStoreApps keep the previous Photos app.
claims.quote: Searched: "Photos" "DisableStoreApps" "previous". Opened MC1518030 and https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-applicationmanagement; neither guarantees retention of the old app, and the notice also covers removed apps.
claims.fix: Remove ', so those devices keep the previous Photos app'. Retain only: 'If DisableStoreApps is set, the notice says the update will not be installed on affected devices.'

claims.claim: The OneDrive photos shown in Photos are stored in OneDrive.
claims.quote: Moments: For photos saved in OneDrive, revisit memories with

claims.claim: The notice does not specify the roles required to configure each policy.
claims.quote: Searched: required administrator roles throughout the full supplied MC1518030 notice. It names existing management controls and recommendations but specifies no administrator role.

claims.claim: The Intune creation path is Devices > Configuration > Create > Configuration settings > Add settings > OneDrive.
claims.quote: 4. Select Create. 5. In Basics, enter the following properties: ... 6. Select Next. 7. In Configuration settings, select Add settings.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Devices > Configuration > Create > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog > Create > Basics > Next > Configuration settings > Add settings > OneDrive'. In the note say 'In Basics, enter a Name before selecting Next.' These are the intervening steps documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/configure-sync-intune; the existing note about creating a profile first does not match a path that starts by creating one.

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync is enabled by setting the HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive registry DWORD DisablePersonalSync to 1.
claims.quote: Enabling this policy sets the following registry key value to 1: [HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisablePersonalSync"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync can be configured through Group Policy or Intune.
claims.quote: Prevent users from syncing personal OneDrive accounts; Applies to: Group Policy, Intune

claims.claim: DisablePersonalSync is a user-scope registry value.
claims.quote: User Configuration policies; [HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive]"DisablePersonalSync"=dword:00000001

claims.claim: The Group Policy location for DisableStoreApps is Windows Components > Store under Computer Configuration.
claims.quote: Name | DisableStoreApps; Friendly Name | Disable all apps from Microsoft Store; Location | Computer Configuration; Path | Windows Components > Store

claims.claim: The device OMA-URI ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ApplicationManagement/DisableStoreOriginatedApps with integer value 1 disables Store app launch.
claims.quote: ./Device/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/ApplicationManagement/DisableStoreOriginatedApps; Format | int; 1 | Disable launch of apps.

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps turns off launch of all preinstalled or downloaded Microsoft Store apps, not just Photos.

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps also stops Microsoft Store apps from being updated.
claims.quote: Apps won't be updated. Your Store will also be disabled.

claims.claim: The cited Learn description says this Store policy applies only to Enterprise and Education editions of Windows.
claims.quote: This setting applies only to Enterprise and Education editions of Windows.

claims.claim: DisableStoreApps is a computer-scope policy.
claims.quote: Location | Computer Configuration

claims.claim: The Lists policy Prevent Lists sync from running on this device has policy name DisableListSync but registry value name DisableNucleusSync.
claims.quote: (DisableListSync) Prevent Lists sync from running on this device; This policy's registry value name DisableNucleusSync differs from the policy name DisableListSync.

claims.claim: The documented DisableNucleusSync setting affects Lists sync on the device.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, Lists sync will be blocked from running on the device.

claims.claim: The Lists sync policy page does not mention Photos.
claims.quote: Searched: Photos in the full fetched text of https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/lists-sync-policies. The page documents Lists sync and DisableNucleusSync, with no mention of Photos.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The governance checklist tells readers to update AppLocker rules, but the controls table has no AppLocker row.
claims.quote: Review any AppLocker packaged-app rule that blocks Microsoft Photos and add the package Microsoft.OneDrive.Photos if the block should stay. The table contains only DisablePersonalSync and DisableStoreApps.
claims.fix: Remove the AppLocker configuration instruction from the Before rollout checklist; retain the existing explanation of Microsoft's AppLocker recommendation in Why it matters and Governance controls. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
